title: Moonlighter 开发商因担心 AI 克隆推迟新作公开测试
content:
Digital Sun delays ReVamp playtest over AI cloning concerns
Programming
PC
Marketing
News
Moonlighter developer delays public playtest of next game over concerns of AI cloning
Digital Sun Games is narrowing its early testing of ReVamp to its Discord community following fears of generative AI-enabled cloning.
Bryant Francis
,
Senior Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
October 19, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Image via Digital Sun
A recent burst of generative AI-enabled game cloning is forcing established game studios to adjust their development strategies—and in one notable indie studio's case, it means scaling back a previously-planned public playtest for fear of being beat to market by vibe-coding copycats.
Said indie studio is
Digital Sun Games
, best known for
Moonlighter
and
Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault
. The company is working on an upcoming "Tower Defensevania" game called
ReVamp
, and had announced plans earlier this month to
host a public playtest
to solicit player feedback, gather metrics, and improve the upcoming game.
Now however, those plans are on ice. In a post on
Steam
and
Bluesky
, the studio informed players that the team is "concerned by recent news of games being reverse-engineered, cloned, and published before the original is even out." (via
Kotaku.
)
"With launch still months away, a large public build of
ReVamp
felt like too big a risk," the company said. It will run a "more contained" playtest through its Discord server starting on October 29.
Related:
RocketWerkz' C# framework 'BRUTAL' is now available to all developers
Digital Sun isn't the only studio to cancel promotional plans for fear of AI cloning. Just yesterday, Alliance Arts and Who's You canceled the Steam Next Fest demo for the upcoming game
Drunken Goddess Reflux
.
Fast-follow video game clones aren't a new phenomenon. Veteran game industry professionals will recall how Vlambeer's
Ridiculous Fishing
and Asher Vollmer, Greg Wohlwend, and BigGiantCircles'
Threes!
were rapidly copied on mobile platforms as early as 2013. But indie developers on watering holes on platforms
like Reddit
have spent the last month describing how scurrilous developers have fed demos, trailers, and images of their games into generative AI tools and quickly rebuilt their basic features from the ground up.
This has all been made possible by longstanding
limited copyright protections
for video game mechanics and advancements in certain LLMs like Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT. Said tools have also been recently deployed to decompile older games, driving a new burst of
vibe-coded mods
.
Digital Sun Studios' announcement highlights how these predatory cloning practices risk harming the market potential for smaller studios looking to break out and build an audience—and how it may require platform owners like Steam to set new policies that disincentivize this behavior. "Showing games early is how indies get seen and find the fans who keep us going," the company wrote. "We hope platforms keep strengthening protections for original work."
